findings.title: Light-theme value changed from 30% to 70%, and the dark-theme value is inverted too.
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. This line now uses 70% for light themes, so poster names in topic meta data turn much paler on the default light theme. The dark branch also uses 30% where every other mapping uses 100 − X, which here would be 70%. The values look swapped. Use `(…$primary 30%, …$secondary 70%)`.

findings.title: Light-theme color for group member names changed from 30% to 50%.
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The light branch now uses 50%, so light themes look different even though the change is only meant to affect dark themes. Keep 30% for light and use the matching 70% for `$secondary`.

findings.title: Lightness values are swapped: the light theme gets 30% where it had 70%.
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, and the desktop counterpart in `desktop/modal.scss` correctly uses (70%, 30%). Here the values are reversed. On light themes the de-emphasised hint text becomes much darker, and on dark themes it becomes overly bright. Use (70%, 30%).

findings.title: Light-theme h3 color changed from 20% to 50% lightness.
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, and the desktop counterpart keeps (20%, 80%). The light branch now uses 50%, so mobile topic-map headings get lighter on light themes, which this change was not meant to do. Use (20%, 80%).

findings.title: Light-theme color for group member names changed from 30% to 50% (mobile).
findings.body: This is the same mistake as on desktop. The original 30% lightness is replaced by 50% in the light branch, which changes how light themes look. Use (30%, 70%).
